name: Onboarding-tour completion-state store
purpose: Owns the completion-state store contract: the writer the step runner calls on the last step, the reader first-run detection calls on principal load, and the clearer the restart-tour control calls. Delegates to the applied persistence blueprint when server-side-per-principal is elicited (and refuses at apply if no persistence blueprint is applied); falls back to spa-local-storage per Q4 or spa-session-storage per the elicit.
responsibilities: Write the completion record on the last step (AC-26104-1).
Read the completion record on principal load so first-run detection can gate the tour auto-open (AC-26105-1).
Clear the completion record when the restart-tour control fires (AC-26104-1, AC-26106-1).
Refuse at apply when server-side-per-principal is elicited without an applied persistence blueprint.
internalStructure: One completion-store module with three backends (spa-local-storage, spa-session-storage, server-side-per-principal) selected at apply time from the elicited completion-state-store answer or the Q4 fallback (spa-local-storage). The server-side backend calls the applied persistence blueprint's writer through the projects own adapter interface; the two SPA backends read and write window.localStorage / window.sessionStorage under a namespaced key derived from the applied blueprint set version.

interfaces.name: completionStore
interfaces.description: { read(principalId): CompletionRecord | null, write(principalId, record), clear(principalId) }. CompletionRecord = { completedAt: ISO string, blueprintSetVersion: string, stepIds: string[] }. The blueprintSetVersion is the versioned identifier of the applied blueprint set so a dismiss-until-next-major or dismiss-until-next-minor policy can re-open the tour on the right bump.

dependencies.name: Persistence blueprint
dependencies.description: server-side-per-principal delegates to the applied persistence blueprint's writer. spa-local-storage and spa-session-storage need no persistence blueprint.

tradeoffs: spa-local-storage is chosen as the Q4 default because a per-session tour that re-plays on every new session is worse than a one-time tour that persists across sessions on that browser; spa-session-storage remains an option for a project that deliberately wants a per-session tour. server-side-per-principal is chosen when the tour completion is a real profile fact (a cross-device onboarding) rather than a per-browser convenience.
notes: The blueprintSetVersion in the CompletionRecord is what lets ADR-2701's dismiss-until-next-major and dismiss-until-next-minor policies re-open the tour on the right bump. Known mechanism-reach gap: the server-side-per-principal backend cannot prove a round-trip in a unit test without an applied persistence blueprint; the pack skips the persistence round-trip check for spa-* stores (inspects the storage directly) and drives it for server-side-per-principal on the fixture branch that stands up an in-fixture writer.
